President Trump said he would allow up to 300,000 metric tons of beef to be imported into the US with lower tariffs over the next 90 days.
News outlets across the political spectrum noted Republican pushback and concern from cattle ranchers.on Friday, Trump blamed high beef prices and a shrinking cattle herd on the Biden administration, and said he the 90-day plan will allow more ground beef imports. Trump didn't share which countries the US is receiving beef from, but told reporters"there are a few" and later mentioned Argentina would be one.
He said the beef would be sold at 25% below current market price.the US cattle herd is at its lowest number in 75 years. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, beef prices have risen over 11% in the last year.said"even MAGA members breaking with the president.
" It cited criticism from Republican lawmakers and rancher associations, and included a quote from Rep. Thomas Massie who called the plan"worse than socialism.
" In a, former CBS News anchor Dan Rather said the idea"is so half-baked that even most ardent supporters are crying foul. "analyzed where the beef might come from, but noted that more than 80% of American beef is produced in the US, so"even an increase in beef imports is unlikely to radically increase the supply of beef and lower prices.
" Rather also said Trump can't guarantee the imports will lower beef prices by 25%.a Georgia cattle rancher who said the move was"pitting the farmer against the consumer" as"cattlemen lose profits for the next three months at the same rate the beef is being discounted. "that the US would import a batch of beef that China rejected in March after finding the presence of an antibiotic, chloramphenicol, which is banned in multiple countries, including China and the US.on theories suggesting a link between the imported beef and the Trump administration's recent move to slaughter wild horses for meat.
The outlet noted horse slaughterhouses are illegal in the US, but wrote that some believe horse meat is being sold to the US for consumption. President Donald Trump on Friday announced a plan to allow more beef imports into the U.S., saying it would reduce consumer costs and help ranchers replenish dwindling cattle herds. President Donald Trump announced a new deal to address the rising cost of beef, support American ranchers, and rebuild the smallest herd in modern history. Reason
